One hot afternoon a great Lion lay asleep in the shade of a tree.
A tiny Mouse was running home through the grass with a berry for her supper.
Pitter, patter, pitter, patter, went her little feet.
She did not see the Lion, and she ran right over his nose.
The Lion woke up with a roar.
He put his big paw down beside the little Mouse.
Who dares to wake the king of the beasts?
said Lion.
You gave me such a fright!
The Mouse stood up on her back legs and held her paws together.
Please let me go, great Lion,
said Mouse.
I did not mean to wake you. If you are kind to me today, I will be kind to you one day.
The Lion laughed so hard that his tummy shook.
You, help me?
You are far too small to help a lion!
But he was a kind king, and he lifted his paw.
Run home, little Mouse,
Some days later the Lion went for a walk by the river.
A yellow butterfly fluttered past his nose, and he bounced after it.
He was having so much fun that he did not look where he was going.
An old fishing net hung between two trees, drying in the sun.
Bump!
The Lion ran right into it.
The net wrapped all around him, from his nose to the tip of his tail.
The Lion wriggled this way and that way.
But the more he wriggled, the more tangled he got.
Grr! This is no fun at all!
Then he gave a big, grumpy roar.
The Mouse heard the roar from far away.
She sat up in her little nest and listened.
That is the kind Lion,
He sounds stuck!
Now it is my turn to be kind to him.
She ran through the grass as fast as her legs could go.
Do not worry, great Lion,
I am coming!
The Mouse stood beside the net and looked up at the Lion.
You came!
But you are so small.
How can you help me?
Just wait and see,
The Mouse began to nibble the ropes with her sharp little teeth.
Nibble, nibble, snip!
She nibbled and nibbled, and one by one the ropes came apart.
Soon there was a hole in the net, and the Lion stepped out.
He shook his mane, and bits of string flew everywhere.
Hooray!
The Lion lay down in the grass, nose to nose with the little Mouse.
Thank you, little friend,
I am sorry I laughed at you.
Now I know that even a small friend can be a great friend.
Kind friends help each other,
said Mouse with a smile.
That evening the Lion lay down under his shady tree, and the Mouse curled up on his big soft paw.
Goodnight, little friend,
Goodnight, great friend,
From that day on, the Lion and the Mouse were the best of friends.
